title: Change a mini centrifuge to its strip rotor: turn it onto the pin, click it on, load
instruction: Get the mini centrifuge ready to spin the two PCR strips: tube rotor off onto the bench, strip rotor clicked on, the strips in opposite slots and the lid latched.
context: Lab automation (Other): PCR set-up is among the commonest wet-lab jobs; a mini centrifuge sits on nearly every PCR bench to spin liquid down before cycling; switching rotors and loading it is a routine hand step. The Corning LSE 6770 ships with an 8-tube rotor and a 4-strip rotor; its maker lists a 'quick release rotor system' that 'eliminates the need for tools', and its manual says to place the other rotor 'into position' on the shaft and snap it in. The hard part is the change, all of it visible on the video: the old rotor comes off only by a straight pull on its 22 mm hub down in the chamber, under the open lid. The new rotor set on the shaft sits 8 mm high on the drive pin and will not go on; it has to be turned on the shaft until it drops about 3 mm onto the snap, then pushed square until it clicks flush. Strips go in an opposite pair, and the lid comes down last: on the real unit shutting it starts the run.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights from the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them; arm bases at y +305 and -305 mm. (1) A Corning LSE mini microcentrifuge, cat. 6770 (white body, smoked see-through lid; 174 x 148 x 122 mm, 1.1 kg; about 320 USD list, both rotors included, listed in stock by US distributors in Nov 2026), unplugged, loose on four rubber feet, its motor shaft at x 150, y 0, the 174 mm side along y, front toward the robot (front face at x 76). The lid is shut and latched and hinges on the top back edge. Its release tab, a 14 x 20 mm lip at the middle of the lid's front edge, frees the lid lock when pressed down 2 mm (about 3 N); the lid then rises to its back stop at 75 degrees in about 0.7 s and stays there. Pressed back down, it latches again. (2) The 8-place tube rotor (6770-RT; 96 mm across, 40 g), empty, snapped on the shaft. (3) The 4-place strip rotor (6770-RTS; 80 x 76 x 20 mm, 110 mm across its corners, 30 g): four parallel slots, 75 x 10 mm and 17 mm deep, 19 and 31 mm each side of the hub; the inner two and the outer two are the opposite pairs. It lies hub up on the table at x 250, y +200, a quarter turn off the shaft's key. Both rotors have the same hub, 22 mm square and 16 mm tall. (4) A white 96-place 0.2 mL PCR rack (127 x 86 x 20 mm) at x 200, y -200, its long side along y. In its columns 4 and 9 (y -222 and -178) stand two Axygen PCR-0208-AF-C strips (eight 0.2 mL tubes at 9 mm pitch, caps closed; 72 x 7 x 21 mm), each along x, each holding eight sealed 20 uL water samples: 1.66 g each, the same mass. Nothing else is on the table. The key and snap as built in the sim: a 16 x 3 mm cross pin through the shaft fits slots under two opposite walls of the hub. More than 10 degrees off the key (two keyed angles, half a turn apart) the hub rests on the pin 8 mm proud; on the key it drops onto two sprung plunger noses, about 4.8 mm proud, and a push of about 3 N snaps it down onto its seat; pulling it off takes about 3 N. Real trials use the real unit as sold. Once per session, before the first trial, the operator checks by hand: (a) the strip rotor set on the shaft out of position does not go on, and turned slowly it drops only at its keyed position(s); (b) a firm straight push then snaps it on with a felt click, and the operator marks the clicked hub-top height on a steel rule; it lifts off by hand; (c) seated, turning it turns the shaft; (d) the tab frees the lid and the lid rises and stays open; (e) the two strips weigh the same within 0.05 g (0.01 g scale). The sim's key, snap and lid are built to behave as (a) to (d) describe. Trials go ahead only if check (a) shows the keyed drop-on: a unit whose rotor goes on at any angle is not used for this task, since the turn onto the drive pin is the task's hard step. Then return everything to the start state above.
scoring: From the poses of the unit, its lid, tab and snap plungers, the rotors and strips, and both grippers. Latch: the lid's catch, shut and latched at the start; the tab pressed 2 mm frees it; it catches again once the lid has opened 3 degrees and is back within 0.6 degrees of shut with the tab up. Latched: caught and the lid within 1 degree of shut. Seated: the strip rotor's hub within 1 mm of the shaft's axis, its underside within 0.5 mm of its seat, tilted under 3 degrees, both plunger noses back out within 0.2 mm (clicked). On shaft: the hub within 2.5 mm of the axis, its underside under 10 mm over its seat, tilted under 8 degrees. Strip in: its middle within 2.5 mm of a slot's middle line and 4 mm along it, its underside within 2 mm of the slot floor, tilted under 10 degrees and turned under 15 degrees from the slot. Balanced: both strips in the two slots of one opposite pair; either strip may go in either slot. Stored: the tube rotor's lowest point within 4 mm of the table top, tilted under 10 degrees, 5 mm or more clear of the unit's footprint. Hands off: over the last 1 s (20 steps) both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from the unit, the rotors and the strips. Score 0 if, at any step, a rotor or strip falls off the table (20 mm under its top), the unit tilts over 10 degrees (tipped), the lid is forced more than 2 degrees off its stop while caught, or, once the lid has been opened and then latched shut, the tab is pressed far enough to free it again (on the real unit that shut started a run); or, at the last step, hands off fails, or the lid is latched with the strip rotor not seated or the load not balanced (unsafe to spin). Otherwise, at the last step: 1.0 seated, balanced, latched and stored; 0.75 seated, balanced and stored, lid not latched; 0.5 seated and stored, not balanced, lid not latched; 0.25 stored and the strip rotor on the shaft but not seated, lid not latched; else 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, same events: a 30 fps phone video from start to end shows drops, hands off, every tab press, lid opening and latching (click, lid down), and the unit's tilt by eye against a square (sliding the upright unit does not count). After the video: lift the lid's front edge with one finger, tab untouched: latched if it stays shut. Press the tab and open the lid. Strips: each cap row level with its slot's top within 2 mm (rule); which slots by eye. Rotor: its hub top within 1 mm of the clicked height marked in the session check (steel rule), a gentle one-finger lift under its rim does not raise it (clicked; an unclicked rotor lifts freely), and turning it turns the shaft. Tube rotor: flat on the table, clear of the unit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; lid and strips opaque; water is mass only; no spin. Drive pin, drop, snap (two sprung sliders) and slots are contact geometry. Lid: sprung hinge, 75 degree stop. Declared rule: the catch. Maker data: unit size and mass, rotor capacities, strip size. Estimates: pin, hub and slot sizes, snap, tab and lid forces, lid timing, part masses; checked on the real unit by the session checks (a) to (e) and the steel-rule click height.
reset_notes: Keep the centrifuge unplugged. Press the tab and open the lid; lift the two strips out into rack columns 4 and 9, caps closed, each along x. Lift the strip rotor off (thumb on top of the shaft, two fingers under the rotor, as the manual says) and lay it hub up on its mark, a quarter turn off the key. Push the tube rotor onto the shaft, turning it until it drops, and press it until it clicks. Shut the lid until it latches and set the unit's feet in their tape marks. Nothing is used up; repeat the operator's checks once per session.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one arm idle: 0.0 left idle, 0.0 right idle)
